Usage:
  redb [command] [options]

  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information
  --version       Show version information

Commands:
  export  Export database to .redb file

result.stdout:
Description:
  Export database to .redb file

Usage:
  redb export [options]

Options:
  -c, --connection <connection> (REQUIRED)  Database connection string
  -p, --provider <provider> (REQUIRED)      Database provider: postgres | mssql | oracle | sqlite
  -o, --output <output> (REQUIRED)          Output file path (.redb)
  --compress                                Compress output file with ZIP
  --schemes <schemes>                       Export only specified scheme IDs (comma-separated): --schemes 100,200,300
  -v, --verbose                             Enable verbose output
  --batch-size <batch-size>                 Batch size for operations (default: 1000) [default: 1000]
  --dry-run                                 Show what would be done without making changes
  -?, -h, --help                            Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Import database from .redb file

Usage:
  redb import [options]

Options:
  -c, --connection <connection> (REQUIRED)  Database connection string
  -p, --provider <provider> (REQUIRED)      Database provider: postgres | mssql | oracle | sqlite
  -i, --input <input> (REQUIRED)            Input file path (.redb)
  --clean                                   Clean database before import
  -j, --parallel <parallel>                 Number of connections to load over (postgres). 1 keeps the whole import in one transaction. More than 1 loads in parallel and rebuilds the secondary indexes of the large tables afterwards: much faster on a large file, but not atomic - a run that fails leaves a partly loaded database to be imported again with --clean. [default: 1]
  -v, --verbose                             Enable verbose output
  --batch-size <batch-size>                 Batch size for operations (default: 1000) [default: 1000]
  --dry-run                                 Show what would be done without making changes
  -?, -h, --help                            Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Export REDB schema SQL script

Usage:
  redb schema [options]

Options:
  -p, --provider <provider> (REQUIRED)  Database provider: postgres | mssql | oracle | sqlite
  -o, --output <output>                 Output file path. If omitted, writes to stdout.
  --upgrade                             Export the upgrade script for an EXISTING database (the versioned SQL module) instead of the full schema. Hand it to the schema owner when the application is not allowed to apply it itself. Idempotent, safe to re-run. Not available for sqlite (the database file upgrades itself).
  -?, -h, --help                        Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Unfold redb objects into flat relational tables and copy the data into them

Usage:
  redb flat [options]

Options:
  -sc, --source-connection <source-connection>         Connection string of the redb database to read
  -sp, --source-provider <source-provider>             Provider of the source database: postgres | mssql | sqlite
  -tc, --target-connection <target-connection>         Connection string of the database that receives the flat tables (may be the source database itself; the tables must not exist yet)
  -tp, --target-provider <target-provider> (REQUIRED)  Provider of the target database: postgres | mssql | sqlite
  -a, --assembly <assembly> (REQUIRED)                 Path to an assembly that declares Props classes. Give several paths, or repeat the option, when the classes live in more than one project. The dependencies of each assembly are resolved from the folder it lies in.
  --types <types>                                      Props classes to unfold, by name or full name (comma-separated). When omitted, every class marked with [RedbScheme] in the given assemblies is taken.
  --ddl-only                                           Print the DDL of the flat tables for the target provider and exit. No database is opened; only --assembly and --target-provider are needed.
  -v, --verbose                                        Enable verbose output
  --batch-size <batch-size>                            Batch size for operations (default: 1000) [default: 1000]
  -?, -h, --help                                       Show help and usage information
